editorial.headline: Veneer Manufacturing Is Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Veneer manufacturing is nationally foreign-open up to 100%, but this record blocks PMA registration in Bali under the province's risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 16212 is a narrow industrial activity: it covers the making of veneer, the thin facing layer described in the record as serutan pelapis, produced by rotary peeling, slicing, or similar methods. The Indonesian scope is compact, but its meaning is exact. This is the manufacturing step itself, not a broader promise about trading, downstream products, or related industries that are not named in the slim record. For a founder, the important discipline is to keep the registration aligned with the recorded act of production: veneer made through peeling, slicing, and comparable processes.

The scale position is broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the code is not presented here as belonging only to one size of operator. That does not create any extra capital figure, threshold, permit, or timeline; the slim record gives scale categories and nothing more. It says this activity can sit across the listed scale ladder, while leaving every other business condition outside the text. The editorial reading should therefore stay clean: the activity is veneer manufacturing, and the record recognises it across all four stated scales.

Nationally, the PMA line is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats this veneer-manufacturing activity as foreign-open up to full foreign ownership. That is the national picture only. It should not be diluted into a maybe-open reading, and it should not be inflated into wider claims about licences, taxes, operational permissions, or processing timeframes that the record does not contain.

Bali changes the answer. The record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and the Bali status as BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, placing the activity inside Bali's PMA moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source named as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. A foreign-owned company may see national openness for KBLI 16212, but it cannot register this activity in Bali under the Bali-side rule recorded here.
